perc_moving_geo20.long_description: Geographic mobility measures the share of a community's population that moved from a different residence in the past year. High mobility rates — sometimes called population churning — can indicate neighborhood instability, weaker social networks, and reduced community investment. As a component of the VDH Health Opportunity Index Built Environment profile, this measure helps characterize the stability and cohesion of a community.
perc_moving_geo20.long_name: Population Moving in the Past Year
perc_moving_geo20.provenance: Directly tabulated from ACS 5-year estimates, table B07204 (Geographical Mobility in the Past Year by Educational Attainment). Percent moving calculated as B07204_003 (moved from different house) divided by B07204_001 (total population 1 year and over). Block group estimates produced via areal interpolation from tract-level data.
perc_moving_geo20.short_description: Percentage of the population that moved from a different residence in the past year.

perc_moving_direct_geo20.long_description: Geographic mobility measures the share of a community's population that moved from a different residence in the past year, estimated at block group level via areal interpolation from tract-level ACS data. This variant provides finer geographic resolution than the tract-level measure for use in composite indices and spatial analysis.
perc_moving_direct_geo20.long_name: Population Moving in the Past Year (block group estimate)
perc_moving_direct_geo20.provenance: Estimated via areal interpolation from tract-level ACS 5-year estimates (table B07204). Tract-level percent moving is redistributed to block groups using area-weighted crosswalks from Census TIGER/Line shapefiles.
perc_moving_direct_geo20.short_description: Population moving in the past year, estimated at block group level via areal interpolation.
